summary: This note describes Loppa, a small island in Loppa Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway, lying in the Lopphavet Sea west of the island of Silda. Its southeastern coast holds a village also called Loppa, once the municipal administrative centre and an important fishing village, though administration has since moved to Øksfjord on the mainland. Loppa Church remains in the village, which has only a few residents left, and a seabird reserve was set up along the western cliffs in 1983.
one_line: Loppa is a sparsely populated island in Loppa Municipality, Finnmark, Norway, with a former fishing village, a church and a seabird reserve.
key_facts: Loppa is an island in Loppa Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway.
The island lies in the Lopphavet Sea in the western part of the municipality.
Loppa lies west of the island of Silda.
The island has one village area, also called Loppa, on its southeastern coast.
The Loppa village used to be the administrative centre of Loppa Municipality.
The Loppa village was an important fishing village for the municipality.
All administration of the Loppa village was moved to Øksfjord on the mainland.
Loppa Church is still located in the village of Loppa.
Only a few residents remain on the island of Loppa.
A seabird reserve was established along the western cliffs of Loppa island in 1983.
